current.text: He is projected to start for Denver next to Jamal Murray, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic.
DeMar DeRozan joined Denver and comes off the bench. If any starter gives up minutes to DeRozan, it will most likely be Braun.
Experts expect him to beat last season's finish outside the top 200. Moore predicts a bounce-back year.
Experts are not buying him at his price. He is called overvalued at a Yahoo ADP of 120, and ranking him in the top 100 would be a mistake.
He made 30% of his threes last season, and defenses have figured him out.
His defense broke down last season, with poor containment and late rotations. He needs to create more steals.
Only 31% of his deflections became steals, so his steals may improve.
He could be traded. Denver may move him instead of Cam Johnson, and Moore expects at least two of last season's starters to be gone by the trade deadline.
Denver plays 43 games through March 28, one below the maximum. They have only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league.

durable.text: He has always been a low-usage player with poor shooting volume. He is not a stat generator.
He hurts his team's spacing, and opponents know it.
His FT% is usually below 80%. The 83% in his breakout year was an outlier.
His FG% around 52% is already good for a perimeter player. The 58% of his breakout year was not real, so little improvement is expected.
His ankle injury last season was more than a sprain. He tore several ligaments.
His finishing depends on athleticism. The ankle injury hurt that athleticism, and his finishing fell off sharply last season.

note: Yahoo ranks him 173 and ESPN ranks him 212, and both value him at 0 USD. That puts him at the edge of or outside our 144-player pool, even though he cost 7 USD in our auction last season. His value comes from a good FG% for a wing (53.7% projected) and few turnovers, with no weak category. The experts still call him overvalued, so take him only as a 1 USD last pick or leave him on waivers.
